result_text:
Template literals are now treated like other string literals when units are compared for duplication, so two functions that differ only inside a `` `...` `` literal are reported as one duplicated unit. I ran the JavaScript, TypeScript and duplication tests in `codeanalyzer`, and they pass.

- **Change:** `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java` now collapses `` `...` `` to ` `` ` before the existing `"..."` and `'...'` handling. It is a single added line.
- **Test:** `JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest` has a new test. Functions differing only in `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` versus `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` are reported as one duplicate. A difference outside the literal (a different `return`) keeps them apart.
- **Limitation:** the replacement works line by line, so a template literal that spans several lines is not collapsed. I did this on purpose, because collapsing across lines would break the mapping back to file line numbers.

I did not commit anything.
